architecture.mechanism: Positioning the catheter tip in a high-flow central venous segment immediately proximal to the cavoatrial junction maintains long-term patency by maximizing hemodynamic washout and preventing thrombus accumulation.
architecture.intervention: Redesign the tunneled hemodialysis catheter with an extended, reinforced shaft and radiopaque markers engineered to place and maintain the distal tip precisely at the cavoatrial junction rather than in smaller tributary veins, ensuring maximum local blood flow velocity across the lumen openings.
architecture.expected_effect: Sustained catheter flow rates above 300 mL/min and pressures below 250 mmHg throughout the device service life due to continuous high-velocity venous flow washing out fibrin precursors before occlusive thrombus can form.
architecture.falsification_test: Conduct a benchtop flow-loop test using bovine blood comparing standard internal jugular tip placement versus cavoatrial junction placement; if the cavoatrial position does not reduce thrombus mass accumulation by at least 50 percent over 72 hours of simulated dialysis cycling while maintaining flow above 300 mL/min, the mechanism is falsified.
